relevance.excluded_scope: Non-binding political statement covering civil applications only (footnote 1); no military AI, no legal obligation, no monitoring or enforcement.
relevance.reason: The concluding political statement of the Paris AI Action Summit, co-chaired by France and India. It sets out shared priorities for inclusive, sustainable and trustworthy AI and endorses the Global Digital Compact's AI governance follow-up, but it is a non-binding statement and creates no legal obligation. It is included because it is the broadest recent intergovernmental statement on AI and because its endorser list documents a visible split among major States.

status_note: Political statement, not a treaty. No signature, ratification or depositary. The official Élysée page, accessed 23 November 2026, lists 65 endorsers (63 States, the European Union and the African Union Commission); the 19 February 2025 PDF lists 64 (62 States plus the two organisations), Zimbabwe appearing only on the later page. Contemporaneous official releases listed 60 endorsers, including South Africa, the United Arab Emirates and the Holy See (listed as “Vatican”), which are absent from the Élysée lists. The statement remains a non-binding declaration; the discrepancy is recorded, not resolved.
